Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.webbrowser

Class FxBrowser

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.webbrowser.FxBrowser
public final class FxBrowser extends Object
The JavaFX half of the browser: one WebView (WebKit) per tab, all created and driven on the JavaFX Application Thread. It owns the tab list (the TabModel) and the parallel WebView map, wires every engine listener (location, title, load progress/state, popups), applies the BrowserSettings (JavaScript, user agent, cookies, zoom, timeouts) and offers robust, cancellable downloads.

All decision logic (failure classification, error-page markup, download naming, find-in-page and reader scripts) lives in JavaFX-free helper classes so it is unit-tested headlessly; this class only marshals threads and drives WebKit. A failed navigation is diagnosed by LoadFailure and rendered as an honest ErrorPage instead of a blank tab, and a per-navigation watchdog cancels loads that stall past the configured page timeout.

This is the only place in the app that touches javafx.scene.web, and it is never constructed in the 3D desktop JVM: there the pure-Swing BrowserPreviewPanel is shown instead and the real browser is spawned into its own child-process JVM (see WebBrowser), so JavaFX never shares a process with the Java 3D OpenGL context.

Every mutating method marshals its work through Platform.runLater(java.lang.Runnable) so the Swing BrowserPanel can call them freely from the EDT. The read-only navigation getters (canGoBack(), getLocation(), getZoom() ...) read a volatile FxBrowser.NavSnapshot refreshed on the FX thread, so the EDT never reaches into WebKit off-thread. State changes are reported back through the FxBrowser.Listener, which fires on the JavaFX thread; the panel re-marshals to the EDT.

    • FxBrowser

      public FxBrowser(FxBrowser.Listener listener, BrowserSettings settings)
      Creates the controller. Call createRoot() on the JavaFX thread afterwards to build the scene graph.
      Parameters:
      listener - the panel to notify (may be null)
      settings - the initial settings (null uses defaults)

  • Method Details

    • setExtensionBroker

      public void setExtensionBroker(ExtensionBroker broker)
      Injects the extension broker that drives the BrowserExtension hooks. May be null (or set later from the panel); while null, the popup / navigate / page-loaded hooks are simply skipped. Called on the EDT before the first load; the field is volatile so the FX thread sees it.
      Parameters:
      broker - the broker, or null to disable extension hooks
